method: Every expectation was written from the sources by reading them. No analysis tool was run on them, and no tool's detectors, source code or output were looked at. Line numbers were looked up by a scratch script that finds the line of a given piece of text and fails unless it occurs exactly once. A second scratch script ran main.js and both preloads in Node against a stand-in for the electron module (and for node:https and node:fs) and printed every ipcMain registration, webContents.send, new BrowserWindow with its merged webPreferences, request (fetch, https.get, net.request), file access, and the channel each exposed member invokes, sends on or listens to, with file:line; its output agreed with the expectations. The renderers were checked by reading only. LANGUAGE: main.js, both preloads and the modules in main/, common/ and preload/ are CommonJS in the shape tsc emits ("use strict", exports.X = ..., enums compiled to an IIFE over Channel, imported functions called as (0, mod_1.fn)(...)); renderer.js, renderer-flasher.js and renderer-diagnostics.js are ES modules, and renderer.js imports renderer/*.js. FILE ATTRIBUTION (as in holdout5): facts are attributed to the source file a reader sees them in. Receivers of table channels name main/ipc-table.js (the table and the loop that calls ipcMain.handle / ipcMain.on are both there). Senders and receivers that go through the IpcClient class name preload.js, where the channel is handed to the client; the ipcRenderer calls themselves are in preload/ipc-client.js (the places lists give both). flash:progress is sent from main/flash-session.js. Every window is created in main/windows.js. In the bundled and minified inputs the modules are bundled into their entry file; bundledFiles maps each module to that file, and line numbers then do not apply. Channel names come from the compiled TypeScript enum Channel (common/ipc-contract.js), from constants exported by other modules (main/flash-session.js FLASH_START, main/telemetry.js TELEMETRY_CHANNEL) and from literals; all are resolvable by evaluating the source, and no channel name is computed at run time. webPreferences lists the keys preload, contextIsolation, nodeIntegration, sandbox, one entry per window and key the code writes (also through SECURE_DEFAULTS and the helper prefsFor); window names the module variable that holds the window; count in an absent entry is one more than the number of windows that have that value, as in holdout4/holdout5. IPC payloads are not a scored class; the object literals sent over IPC are listed under ipcPayloadsUnscored for a reader, and nothing reads them.

present.why: Channel.ListDevices = "device:list" in common/ipc-contract.js (a compiled TypeScript enum). Receiver: an entry { channel: ipc_contract_1.Channel.ListDevices, kind: "handle", run } in the table returned by buildTable (main/ipc-table.js), which registerAll walks, calling ipcMain.handle(entry.channel, ...); buildTable and registerAll are called from main.js. Sender: preload.js member listDevices, client.invoke(ipc_contract_1.Channel.ListDevices, ...) on the IpcClient of preload/ipc-client.js, whose invoke calls ipcRenderer?.invoke(channel, payload). Returns bus.list().

Payload { deviceId }.

Channel.GetSettings = "settings:get" in common/ipc-contract.js (a compiled TypeScript enum). Receiver: an entry { channel: ipc_contract_1.Channel.GetSettings, kind: "handle", run } in the table returned by buildTable (main/ipc-table.js), which registerAll walks, calling ipcMain.handle(entry.channel, ...); buildTable and registerAll are called from main.js. Sender: preload.js member getSettings, client.invoke(ipc_contract_1.Channel.GetSettings, ...) on the IpcClient of preload/ipc-client.js, whose invoke calls ipcRenderer?.invoke(channel, payload). Returns the settings file.

Channel.SetSettings = "settings:set" in common/ipc-contract.js (a compiled TypeScript enum). Receiver: an entry { channel: ipc_contract_1.Channel.SetSettings, kind: "handle", run } in the table returned by buildTable (main/ipc-table.js), which registerAll walks, calling ipcMain.handle(entry.channel, ...); buildTable and registerAll are called from main.js. The patch is the payload.

Channel.CheckFirmware = "firmware:check" in common/ipc-contract.js (a compiled TypeScript enum). Receiver: an entry { channel: ipc_contract_1.Channel.CheckFirmware, kind: "handle", run } in the table returned by buildTable (main/ipc-table.js), which registerAll walks, calling ipcMain.handle(entry.channel, ...); buildTable and registerAll are called from main.js. Sender: preload.js member checkFirmware, client.invoke(ipc_contract_1.Channel.CheckFirmware, ...) on the IpcClient of preload/ipc-client.js, whose invoke calls ipcRenderer?.invoke(channel, payload). Payload { model, channel: track }: the field named channel is the firmware track ("stable" or "beta"), not an IPC channel.

Channel.OpenFlasher = "flasher:open" in common/ipc-contract.js (a compiled TypeScript enum). Receiver: an entry { channel: ipc_contract_1.Channel.OpenFlasher, kind: "on", run } in the table returned by buildTable (main/ipc-table.js), which registerAll walks, calling ipcMain.on(entry.channel, ...); buildTable and registerAll are called from main.js. Sender: preload.js member openFlasher, client.send(ipc_contract_1.Channel.OpenFlasher, ...) on the IpcClient of preload/ipc-client.js, whose send calls ipcRenderer?.send(channel, payload). Fire and forget: kind "on" in the table, client.send in the preload. Opens the flasher window.

exports.FLASH_START = "flash:start" in main/flash-session.js, used as channel: flash_session_1.FLASH_START in the table of main/ipc-table.js (kind handle); a channel constant from another module than the enum. Sender: preload-flasher.js member start, ipcRenderer.invoke("flash:start", { deviceId, model, version }) with the name written out (sandboxed preload)

main.js: on the DeviceBus "attach" event, windows_1.windows.main?.webContents.send(ipc_contract_1.Channel.DeviceAttached, { id, model, firmware }). Receiver: preload.js onDeviceAttached, client.subscribe(Channel.DeviceAttached, listener), whose body calls ipcRenderer.on(channel, wrapped) in preload/ipc-client.js

main/flash-session.js FlashSession.report: this.target.webContents.send("flash:progress", { stage, percent }), target being the flasher window found by BrowserWindow.fromWebContents in the flash:start handler. Receiver: preload-flasher.js onProgress, ipcRenderer.on("flash:progress", ...)
main.js ipc.on("flash:cancel", ...), ipc being const ipc = electron_1.ipcMain (another name for ipcMain). Sender: preload-flasher.js member cancel, ipcRenderer.send("flash:cancel", deviceId)

present.why: main/firmware.js checkFirmware: https.get(feedUrl, { headers }, ...) from node:https, feedUrl = `${FEED_BASE}/${track}.json` with FEED_BASE = "https://firmware.padwright.example/feed"; the track comes from the firmware:check payload (the settings' firmwareTrack, "stable" by default). Called by the firmware:check handler

main/firmware.js downloadImage: electron_1.net.request({ method: "GET", url: `${DOWNLOAD_BASE}/${encodeURIComponent(model)}/${version}.bin` }), DOWNLOAD_BASE = "https://dl.padwright.example/firmware"; model and version come from the flash:start payload. Called by FlashSession.run

main/telemetry.js track: fetch(EVENTS_URL, { method: "POST" }), EVENTS_URL = `${TELEMETRY_ORIGIN}/v2/events` with TELEMETRY_ORIGIN = "https://telemetry.padwright.example"; only when the setting telemetry is on. Called by the telemetry:event listener

renderer/gallery.js browse: fetch(`${GALLERY_API}/layouts?model=${encodeURIComponent(model)}&sort=top`), GALLERY_API = "https://share.padwright.example/api"; the model comes from the attached device. Called from renderer.js showGallery
renderer/gallery.js share: fetch(`${GALLERY_API}/layouts`, { method: "POST", body }); called from the Share button in renderer.js

ipcPayloadsUnscored.note: Not a scored class (the scorer has none for payloads). The object literals sent over each channel, by field name, for a reader. setSettings sends the caller's patch object and flash:cancel sends a bare deviceId; neither is an object literal.
